families.description: Prostrate, erect or rarely climbing annual or perennial herbs, subshrubs, shrubs, or rarely small trees, usually with cystoliths, isophyllous or anisophyllous with the leaf pairs of unequal size at a node. Branches decussate, terete to angular, the nodes often swollen, sometimes spinose with spines derived from reduced leaves, bracts or bracteoles. Stipules absent. Leaves opposite, rarely alternate or whorled; blade margin entire, sinuate, crenate, dentate or rarely pinnatifid. Inflorescences terminal or axillary spikes, racemes, panicles or dense clusters, rarely of solitary flowers; bracts one per flower or dichasial cluster, large and brightly coloured or minute and green, sometimes spinose; bracteoles usually 2 per flower, rarely absent. Flowers sessile or pedicellate, bisexual, zygomorphic to subactinomorphic. Calyx synsepalous at least basally, usually 4- or 5-lobed. Corolla sympetalous, usually 2-lipped. Stamens 2 or 4, epipetalous. Ovary superior, 2-locular. Fruit usually an explosively dehiscent capsule, the seeds borne on hooked retinacula.

families.description: Perennial, glabrous, aromatic herbs growing in marshes or as emergent aquatics; laticifers and raphides absent, aerenchyma present. Rhizome creeping, much branched, lacunose, with specialised aromatic oil cells, rooting on the lower side and bearing leaves at the apex. Leaves distichous with overlapping bases, unifacial, ensiform, not differentiated into petiole and blade; intravaginal squamules present in the leaf axils; venation parallel. Inflorescence solitary, terminal, borne laterally on a leaf-like scape, the peduncle triangular; the so-called spathe much longer than the spadix, erect and persistent, appearing merely as a vertical leaf-like extension; spadix jutting from the peduncle at an angle, sessile, conoid and finger-like or slender and tail-like, flowering from the base upwards. Flowers bisexual, perigoniate, densely arranged, bractless, trimerous; tepals 6 in two whorls of 3, free and thin; stamens 6 in two whorls of 3, free, the filaments linear-oblong and flattened, the anthers introrse and dehiscing by a longitudinal slit; pollen monosulcate.

families.description: Trees, shrubs or woody vines. Leaves alternate, simple, shortly or long petiolate, not stipulate. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, the plants polygamous or functionally dioecious, usually fascicled, cymose or paniculate. Sepals (2 or 3 or)5, imbricate and rarely valvate. Petals (4 or)5 and sometimes more, imbricate. Stamens 10 to numerous, distinct or adnate to the petal bases, hypogynous; anthers 2-celled, versatile, dehiscing by apical pores or longitudinally. Ovary superior, the disk absent, with 3-5 or more locules and axile placentation; ovules 10 or more per locule; styles as many as the carpels, distinct or connate, generally persistent. Fruit a berry or leathery capsule. Seeds not arillate, with usually large embryos and abundant endosperm.

families.description: Perennial herbs of diverse habit, including climbers, floating aquatics, helophytes, pachycaul shrubs and geophytes. Underground stems absent, or rhizomatous or tuberous; aerial stems variously produced or not, often evergreen; bulbils for vegetative reproduction sometimes produced. Leaves alternate or apparently basal, usually petiolate with sheathing bases, often subtended by prophylls and/or cataphylls; blade various - linear, simple with the base often cordate to sagittate, sometimes peltate, or variously compound (pinnate, radiate, pedate or decompound), or more elaborately dissected. Inflorescence consisting of a spadix subtended by a spathe, the spathe commonly with a tube-like base, persistent or with a deciduous blade. Spadix bearing bisexual or unisexual flowers, in the latter case the spadix female below and male above. Bisexual flowers with 0, 4 or 6 tepals; stamens 4-6(-22), the filaments free; ovary usually 3-locular or more, or 1-locular. Unisexual flowers almost always naked: male of 1-6 free stamens or 2-12 stamens connate into a synandrium beneath a common synconnective. Fruit usually a berry.

families.description: Trees, shrubs, lianas, woody epiphytes, or more rarely herbs outside Malesia. Branches usually stout with the leaves clustered at their ends, armed or unarmed, glabrous or with a tomentum of stellate or simple hairs; buds covered either by the stipular sheaths of the leaves or by cataphylls. Leaves spiral, rarely opposite or whorled; petiole usually clasping the stem; stipules distinct, united into a ligule, or absent; lamina digitately compound or pinnate, sometimes to the second or third degree, or simple and then entire or pinnately to palmately lobed, the margin entire or dentate. Inflorescence terminal or more rarely lateral, either simple or compound racemes or spikes, or more commonly of umbels or capitula, solitary or arranged into compound umbels or panicles; bracts usually small and caducous; pedicel articulated with the flower or continuous with it. Flowers hermaphrodite or heterosexual, sometimes dioecious, actinomorphic. Calyx lobes small, reduced to a rim, or rarely absent.

families.description: Monoecious trees, medium-sized to very large, rarely shrubby in strongly exposed situations. Cotyledons four, or two fused pairs, sometimes retained within the seed after germination. The foliage-shoot apex differs between the two genera: a few much-reduced leaves in Araucaria, an organised bud of overlapping scales in Agathis. Leaves varying from scale- or needle-like to broad and leathery with many parallel veins, the different forms sometimes borne on one plant at different stages of growth. Pollen cones cylindrical, 1-20 cm long, solitary, terminal or lateral, borne on branches separate from the seed cones and subtended by modified scale-like leaves, deciduous at maturity; microsporophylls numerous, spirally arranged and stalked, each bearing several to many pendent elongate pollen sacs beneath an expanded shield-like apex. Pollen globose, without bladders. Seed cones large and well formed, terminal on a stout shoot, usually maturing in the second year and disintegrating to release the seeds; bract complexes numerous and spirally placed, each bract leathery to woody and fused to the fertile scale, which bears one large inverted seed on its upper surface, in most cases shed with a wing-like structure.

families.description: Palms with stems solitary or clustered, short and subterranean, erect, or climbing. Leaves pinnate, palmate or costapalmate, spirally or rarely distichously arranged, sometimes spiny; sheaths usually open, sometimes closed and forming a crownshaft, in climbing plants usually with knees and sometimes with flagella; petioles absent to elongate, smooth or spiny, in palmate leaves with a hastula at the apex; rachis short to elongate, absent in palmate leaves, sometimes extended into a whip-like climbing organ or cirrus; pinnae regularly or irregularly arranged along the rachis, variously shaped and mostly reduplicate; segments of palmate leaves variously arranged, single or multi-fold, mostly induplicate. Plants monoecious, sometimes dioecious, iteroparous or less often semelparous. Inflorescences borne among or below the leaves, solitary or rarely multiple at a node; peduncle bearing a prophyll and usually one or more peduncular bracts; rachillae one to many, bearing the flowers solitary, paired, in threes or more. Flowers usually with 3 sepals, 3 petals, 6 stamens and 3 carpels. Fruits variously shaped and coloured, sometimes covered with overlapping scales; endosperm ruminate or homogeneous.

The rattans - climbing palms with knees, flagella and cirri, all described above - are of major economic importance in the Philippines, and 59 of the accepted Philippine species carry a DENR threatened-species listing.

families.description: Perennial herbs, more commonly woody at the base, undershrubs or shrubs, erect, scrambling or scandent, sometimes high lianas. Rhizome not rarely tuberous. Branches often slightly swollen and jointed at the nodes. Hairs simple, uni- or multicellular, the short ones often with a hooked apex. Leaves simple, spiral or alternate, petioled without an abscission zone, exstipulate; nervation commonly palmate, or pinnate with the nerves often extending obliquely towards the margin. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic or zygomorphic, solitary, fascicled, or in axillary or cauligerous racemose, paniculate or cymose inflorescences, usually only one or two open at a time; bracts present and often persistent; pedicel often hardly distinct from the ovary. Calyx petaloid, gamosepalous, 3- or 6-lobed or 1-lipped, the lobes valvate or induplicate. Petals absent in Malesian species. Stamens 6, or 6 to about 36(-46), in one whorl or in two to four whorls in Thottea; filaments free or slightly united at the base, and/or almost wholly adnate to the style column to form a gynostemium; anthers free in Thottea or dorsally united with the style column in Aristolochia, each of 2 thecae with 4 pollen sacs, extrorse.

families.description: Herbs, subshrubs or shrubs, rarely trees or climbers, bisexual, monoecious or sometimes dioecious, many with laticiferous cells or canals and/or resin ducts. Leaves often in a basal rosette, the cauline leaves usually alternate and more rarely opposite or whorled, sessile or petiolate, without stipules; blade entire to variously lobed or divided. Florets bisexual, female, or functionally male, solitary or few to many enclosed in an involucre of one- to many-seriate phyllaries to form a capitulum; an outer calyculus of bracts sometimes present. Capitula solitary or few to many in variously formed synflorescences, homogamous or heterogamous, discoid, disciform, radiate or ligulate; receptacle usually flattened, smooth or alveolate, with or without scales, bristles or hairs. Corolla (3-)5-merous, gamopetalous, tubular or tubular-filiform and regular, or bilabiate, radiate or ligulate. Stamens (4 or)5, inserted within the corolla tube, the filaments adnate to it; anthers usually coalescent into a tube around the style, the apex usually with a sterile appendage. Style apically bifid, the branches variously shaped. Ovary inferior, 1-locular; ovule 1, basal. Fruit an achene (cypsela). Pappus of one to many rows of scales or bristles, or absent.

Flowers pedicellate or sessile, subtended by bracts.

families.description: Annual or perennial herbs. Stems erect or procumbent, usually succulent, often rooting at the lower nodes. Leaves simple, alternate, opposite or verticillate, not stipulate or sometimes with stipular glands at the petiole base, pinnately veined, the margin serrate to nearly entire with the teeth often glandular-mucronate. Flowers bisexual, protandrous, zygomorphic, resupinate through 180 degrees, in axillary or subterminal racemes or pseudo-umbels, or fascicled or solitary. families.description: Perennial succulent herbs, very rarely subshrubs. Stem erect and frequently rhizomatous, or the plants tuberous and either acaulescent or shortly stemmed, rarely lianoid or climbing with adventitious roots, or stoloniferous. Leaves simple, rarely palmately compound, alternate or all basal, petiolate; stipules usually deciduous; blade often oblique and asymmetric and rarely symmetric, the margin irregularly serrate and divided or occasionally entire, the venation usually palmate. Flowers unisexual, the plants monoecious and rarely dioecious, borne in dichotomous cymes of (1 or)2-4 to several, rarely numerous, sometimes in panicles. Staminate flowers with 2 or 4 decussate tepals, the outer usually larger; stamens usually numerous, the filaments free or connate at the base; anthers 2-celled. Pistillate flowers with 2-5(-10) usually free tepals; ovary nodding, pendulous or ascending, 1-3- and rarely 4-8-locular; placentation axile or parietal; styles 2 or 3 or more, free or fused at the base, forked once or more; stigmas turgid, spirally twisted, U-shaped, or capitate to reniform and setose-papillose. Capsule dry and sometimes berry-like, unequally or subequally 3-winged, rarely wingless and 3- or 4-horned. Seeds very numerous and minute, the testa pale brown and reticulate.

families.description: Dioecious, rarely monoecious trees or shrubs. Bark of the twigs with a whorl of resiniferous ducts bordered outwardly by a distinct, closed or more or less interrupted sinuous sclerenchymatic cylinder. Pith of twigs, petioles and petiolules not rarely with vascular strands. Leaves imparipinnate, sometimes 1-foliolate, spirally arranged and very rarely in pseudowhorls, usually more or less crowded at the ends of the branchlets. Stipules absent except in Garuga and Canarium, and in Garuga stipels are often present as well. Inflorescences paniculate, tending towards racemes or spikes when poor, axillary and often crowded at the ends of the branchlets, sometimes pseudoterminal or terminal. Bracts and bracteoles usually deltoid to subulate. Flowers 3-5-merous, generally greenish to creamy, usually unisexual with remains of the other sex.

families.description: Fleshy perennials, shrubs, trees or vines, terrestrial or epiphytic. Stems jointed, terete, globose, flattened or fluted, mostly leafless and variously spiny. Leaves alternate, flat or subulate to terete, vestigial or entirely absent; the spines, glochids and flowers always arising from cushion-like axillary areoles, which are modified short shoots and are the defining structure of the family. Flowers solitary and sessile, rarely clustered and stalked in Pereskia, bisexual and rarely unisexual, actinomorphic or occasionally zygomorphic. Receptacle tube absent or short to elongate, naked or invested with leaf-like bracts, scales, areoles, hairs, bristles or spines; perianth segments usually numerous in a sepaloid to petaloid series. Stamens numerous. Ovary inferior, rarely superior, 1-locular with parietal placentation. Fruit usually a berry.
families.philippine_note: CDFP accepts 4 Philippine species in 3 genera (Opuntia, Cereus, Epiphyllum), none endemic. All Philippine members are introduced; the areole is what separates a cactus from any other spiny succulent.

families.description: Annuals, perennials, more rarely shrubs, small trees or vines, mostly laticiferous, sometimes with subterranean tubers. Leaves exstipulate, simple, entire or toothed to incised and rarely pinnatifid, spirally arranged or alternate, rarely opposite. Flowers often blue, violet, red or white, frequently protandrous, axillary or terminal, solitary or in mostly bracteate racemose inflorescences, bisexual and rarely unisexual, isomerous. Disk epigynous, mostly free. Ovary inferior or partly so, rarely superior, 2-5-celled. Style 1, often with hairs below the 2-5 stigmatic lobes. Ovules many, mostly on axile placentas. Fruit a capsule or a berry, mostly dehiscing at the apex by valves, or circumscissile. Seeds many; embryo straight; albuminous.

families.description: Annual or perennial herbs, erect or twining, dioecious or sometimes monoecious, often with cystoliths. Stems furrowed or winged. Stipules free. Leaves alternate or opposite, palmately lobed or compound, sometimes simple. Male inflorescences a bracteate cymose panicle; male flowers pedicellate with 5 free sepals, no petals, and 5 stamens opposite the sepals, the anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits. Female inflorescences a bracteate spicate cyme; female flowers sessile, the calyx appressed to the ovary and membranous, petals absent; ovary 1-locular with a solitary pendulous ovule; style 2-parted with filiform branches. Fruit an achene covered by the persistent calyx; embryo curved or spirally involute.

families.description: Shrubs, trees or woody vines, evergreen, with branched or simple trichomes. Stipules spine-like, small, or absent. families.description: Annual or perennial herbs, rarely dwarf shrubs or small bushes. Stems often thickened at the nodes. Leaves opposite, rarely spirally arranged, sometimes apparently whorled, entire, often connate at the base; stipules present or more commonly absent. families.description: Evergreen trees or shrubs, monoecious or dioecious. Ultimate branchlets jointed, slender and ridged, consisting of several short basal articles and one to many elongated articles, often pubescent when young - the green branchlets, not the leaves, carry out photosynthesis. Leaves small and tooth-like, in whorls of 4 to about 20, equal in number to the ridges on the branchlet; stipules absent. Inflorescences spike-like or head-like, with alternating whorls of tooth-like bracts, a single flower within each bract with two lateral scale-like bracteoles. Flowers unisexual, without pedicels. Male inflorescences terminal or lateral terete slender spikes; male flowers with 1 or 2 scale-like deciduous tepals and a single stamen. Female inflorescences head-like, globose or ellipsoid, usually terminal on short lateral branches; female flowers without a perianth. Infructescence woody and cone-like, the samaras released between the hardened bracteoles.

families.description: Trees or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate, often coriaceous, glabrous or with an indumentum beneath, the margin entire; petioles often with 2 lateral glands. Stipules 2, minute and caducous to large and persistent, usually linear-lanceolate. Inflorescence racemose, paniculate or cymose; flowers bracteate and usually bibracteolate. Flowers actinomorphic to zygomorphic, hermaphrodite or rarely polygamous, markedly perigynous. Receptacle campanulate to cylindrical or rarely flattened and cupuliform, often gibbous at the base; calyx lobes 5, imbricate and often unequal. Petals 5, inserted on the margin of the disk, commonly unequal, imbricate, deciduous. Stamens indefinite, 2-60, inserted on the disk margin in a complete circle or unilaterally, all fertile or some reduced to tooth-like staminodes; filaments free or ligulately connate, short and included to long and far exserted; anthers small, 2-locular, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary basically of three carpels but usually with only one developed, the others aborted or vestigial.

description.text: Trees or shrubs. Leaves simple, alternate, often coriaceous, glabrous or with an indumentum beneath, the margin entire; petioles often with 2 lateral glands. Stipules 2, minute and caducous to large and persistent, usually linear-lanceolate. Inflorescence racemose, paniculate or cymose; flowers bracteate and usually bibracteolate. Flowers actinomorphic to zygomorphic, hermaphrodite or rarely polygamous, markedly perigynous. Receptacle campanulate to cylindrical or rarely flattened and cupuliform, often gibbous at the base; calyx lobes 5, imbricate and often unequal. Petals 5, inserted on the margin of the disk, commonly unequal, imbricate, deciduous. Stamens indefinite, 2-60, inserted on the disk margin in a complete circle or unilaterally, all fertile or some reduced to tooth-like staminodes; filaments free or ligulately connate, short and included to long and far exserted; anthers small, 2-locular, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary basically of three carpels but usually with only one developed, the others aborted or vestigial.

families.description: Trees or shrubs, evergreen in the Malesian species; leaf scars large. Leaves crowded towards the ends of the shoots, spiral, simple, exstipulate, serrate with glandular teeth and often with an apical gland, more rarely entire; nerves a little decurrent along the midrib, both midrib and nerves somewhat impressed above and prominent beneath. Indumentum of the branchlets, leaves and inflorescences of simple and/or long fascicled patent and/or minor depressed stellate hairs. Flowers bisexual, regular, 5(-6)-merous. Inflorescences sometimes simple solitary terminal racemes, but mostly a terminal raceme with several lower approximate racemes each from the axil of a reduced or caducous leaf, together forming a panicle-, fascicle- or umbel-like inflorescence. Calyx lobes 5(-6), persistent, quincuncially imbricate, united only at the base. Petals 5(-6), generally free, alternating with the calyx lobes, rather early caducous, generally sweet-scented. Stamens 10(-12) in 2 whorls of 5(-6), the filaments adnate to the corolla at the extreme base; anthers dorsifixed, overturned outwards in bud.

families.description: Trees, shrubs or lianas, rarely subherbaceous. Glands often present on the leaf bases or petioles and in the lower marginal crenations in Malesian species. Indumentum of simple hairs, glandular hairs, or multicellular hairs secreting calcium oxalate and forming scales, or present beneath the cuticle so that the leaf surface is minutely verruculose and sometimes pellucid-punctate. Leaves opposite, verticillate, spiral or alternate, petioled and rarely sessile, exstipulate, simple, almost always entire. Flowers usually protogynous and usually actinomorphic, rarely slightly zygomorphic, in axillary or extra-axillary elongated or subcapitate spikes or racemes, or in terminal and sometimes axillary panicles. Receptacle usually in two distinct parts: a lower receptacle surrounding and adnate to the inferior ovary, and an upper receptacle produced beyond it into a short or long tube terminating in the calyx lobes. Calyx lobes 4 or 5, rarely 6-8, or almost absent, sometimes accrescent. Petals 4 or 5 or absent, conspicuous or very small, inserted near the mouth of the upper receptacle. Stamens usually twice as many as the petals, borne inside the upper receptacle usually in two series, exserted or included.

families.description: Annual or perennial herbs, sometimes woody at the base. Stems with prominent nodes and internodes. Leaves alternate, distichous or spirally arranged, sessile or petiolate; leaf sheath prominent, open or closed; blade simple and entire. Inflorescence usually of cincinni in panicles or solitary, sometimes shortened into heads, sometimes sessile with the flowers fascicled, sometimes axillary and penetrating the enveloping leaf sheath. Flowers bisexual and rarely unisexual, actinomorphic or zygomorphic, typically lasting a single morning. Sepals 3, free or connate at the base, often boat-shaped or keeled. Petals (2 or)3, free, sometimes connate and tubular in the middle, sometimes clawed. Stamens 6, free, all or only 2 or 3 fertile; filaments glabrous or bearded with moniliform hairs; anthers dehiscing longitudinally or rarely by apical pores; staminodes often present. Ovary superior, 2- or 3-locular. Fruit usually a capsule.

families.description: Herbs or shrubs, sometimes parasitic, usually with twining stems, occasionally prostrate, creeping or erect, very rarely trees, often with milky juice. Leaves mostly spirally arranged, absent or nearly so in parasitic species, usually petioled, the petiole sometimes with extrafloral nectaries. Stipules absent. Inflorescences mostly cymose, one- to many-flowered, with mostly opposite or subopposite bracts at the base of the cymes or beneath the solitary flowers; rarely racemose. Flowers generally hermaphrodite, actinomorphic, rarely slightly zygomorphic, usually 5-merous, various in size and colour, often showy. Sepals usually free, imbricate with quincuncial aestivation, often persistent, sometimes accrescent in fruit. Corolla sympetalous, often funnel-shaped or campanulate, more rarely rotate, salver-shaped or urceolate, the limb nearly entire to deeply lobed, often contorted-plicate in bud. Stamens isomerous, alternating with the corolla lobes and adnate to the corolla, the filaments usually slender; anthers dehiscing introrsely or laterally and longitudinally. Disk mostly present, annular or cupular.

families.description: Shrubs, rarely perennial herbs with herbaceous stems, or small trees. Roots with nodules containing nitrogen-fixing bacteria. Innovations in flushes from perulate apical buds. Branches 4-angular with alternating ridges; xylem with broad medullary rays. Leaves generally small, sessile or subsessile with a narrow joint at the base, simple, entire, cordate-ovate to lanceolate, acute, decussate, the phyllotaxis of lateral branches mostly appearing pseudo-distichous; blades palmately 3-9-curvinerved and net-veined. Stipules absent. Racemes terminal or axillary. Flowers in the axils of small bracts, greenish or reddish, actinomorphic, hypogynous, polygamous. Perianth 5-merous; sepals 5, imbricate, persistent, ovate; petals 5, alternate, shorter than the sepals, keeled inside, accrescent and becoming more or less fleshy, each enveloping a carpel in fruit. Stamens 10 in two whorls, free, or those opposite the petals adnate to the petal keel; anthers exserted.

families.description: Perennial terrestrial herbs, NOT aromatic - the character that most readily separates them from the gingers - with more or less fleshy rhizomes. Stems usually simple, often long and terete and sometimes spirally contorted, leafy. Leaves spirally arranged, those toward the stem base usually bladeless; leaf sheath tubular and closed; ligule present; petiole short; blade narrowly to broadly elliptic, rolled longitudinally in bud, the margin entire. Inflorescence a cone-like spike, terminal on leafy shoots or on separate short leafless shoots from the rhizome; bracts imbricate, with a linear nectariferous callus below the apex, 1- or 2-flowered. Flowers bisexual, epigynous, zygomorphic. Calyx tubular, 2- or 3-lobed. Corolla tubular below, 3-lobed above, the lobes unequal. Staminodes 5, united into a labellum equalling or much longer than the corolla. Ovary inferior. Fruit a capsule.

families.description: Herbs or undershrubs, usually succulent, perennial, less often annual or biennial. Leaves spirally arranged, opposite or whorled, exstipulate, simple or compound, entire, dentate, crenate, serrate or deeply incised. Flowers usually bisexual and rarely unisexual, actinomorphic, usually in cymes or cymose panicles, rarely spicate or solitary in the leaf axils, mostly 4-5- and rarely 3- or polymerous. Sepals free or nearly so, or united into a distinct tube, marcescent and persistent after anthesis as are the petals. Petals as many as the sepals, rarely more, hypogynous, free or variously connate. Stamens either as many as the petals and alternating with them, or twice their number, perigynous or inserted wholly or partly on the corolla; filaments free; anthers 2-celled, the cells introrse and dehiscing longitudinally. Hypogynous scales as many as the carpels, placed singly behind them. Carpels superior, as many as the petals, epipetalous, free or connate at the base, 1-celled; ovules mostly many and biseriate. Styles as many as the carpels, free. Fruit a follicle, membranous or leathery, opening on the adaxial side. Seeds minute.

families.description: Evergreen trees. Twigs terete to quadrangular, the younger ones mostly with four narrow ribs or wings, the nodes thickened and the petiole bases mostly connected by a faint line. Leaves with minute or rudimentary stipules, opposite, simple, entire, penninerved, shortly petioled, the nerves arched or almost straight and mostly anastomosing into a marginal vein. Inflorescence terminal or axillary. Flowers bisexual or sometimes unisexual by reduction and the trees then dioecious, actinomorphic, peri- to epigynous, (4-)5(-6)-merous, sometimes with twice as many stamens; receptacle widely campanulate. Sepals valvate, triangular to deltoid, mostly persistent. Petals more or less rudimentary, sometimes absent, alternisepalous.

families.description: Tree, 12-40 m tall and 15-120 cm in diameter, buttressed. Twigs with distinct leaf scars, thickened at the insertion of the buds, glabrous; innovations marginally and apically tufted-hairy. Stipules boat-shaped, triangular to ovate, 1.5-2.5(-3) mm long, entire, the apex rounded to emarginate. Leaves glabrous, narrowly ovate to elliptic and sometimes obovate, often with more or less parallel margins, 5-15 by 2-6 cm; base broadly cuneate to rounded; margin often somewhat thickened; apex broadly acute to obtusely acuminate; nerves (5-)7-10(-12) pairs, curving slightly upwards near the margin and often meeting in one or two looped intramarginal veins. Inflorescence branched, broadly ovoid to depressed obovoid, 3-9(-16) cm long, the axes patently tufted-hairy especially above the nodes; bracts caducous just below the articulation, more or less boat-shaped, with a row of bristles within at the base. Pedicel articulate, grooved, swollen in fruit. Hypanthium thickened. Sepals appressed, boat-shaped, obovate to depressed ovate, with a row of bristles at the inner base.

families.description: Woody plants, from small shrubs to tall upper-canopy trees, rarely hemi-epiphytes and stranglers, evergreen or rarely deciduous. Twigs generally more or less flattened or angular following the phyllotaxis when young, becoming terete with lenticels and longitudinal fissures. Leaves opposite and decussate, or verticillate in alternate whorls, or rarely alternate, pinnately or palmately compound and usually with a terminal leaflet, or trifoliolate, or simple to unifoliolate; leaflet margins crenate-serrate or entire; venation pinnate. Indumentum generally of simple hairs, occasionally of stellate and peltate trichomes or rarely stinging hairs.

families.description: Dioecious marine plants. Rhizome creeping, either herbaceous, monopodial and rooting at the nodes, or ligneous, sympodial and rooting from the internodes. Scales scarious, ovate or elliptic, marked with small dark longitudinal stripes and dots of tannin cells. Leaves distichous; leaf sheath broad and completely or almost completely amplexicaul, leaving open or closed circular scars when shed, bi-auriculate and ligulate, the scarious flaps covered with numerous short dark stripes and dots; leaf blade linear or subulate with 3 to several parallel nerves, the tip variable in outline. Flowers without a perigone, solitary and either terminal on a short branch or in a cymose inflorescence. Male flowers subsessile or stalked, of 2 quadrilocular extrorsely dehiscent anthers dorsally connate over at least part of their length and attached at the same or slightly different levels; pollen confervoid - filamentous rather than granular, an adaptation to water-borne pollination. Female flowers sessile or shortly stalked.
families.philippine_note: CDFP accepts 6 Philippine species in 5 genera (Halodule, Cymodocea, Oceana, Syringodium, Thalassodendron), none endemic. These are true sea-grasses, and Flora Malesiana notes that although the world total is only 60-65 species, their beds stabilise muddy and sandy coastal substrates and serve as nurseries - which makes this small family disproportionately important in Philippine coastal ecology.

families.description: Annual or perennial herbs, rhizomatous to stoloniferous. Culms simple and often 3-sided - the character that separates sedges from grasses in the field. Leaves basal and/or cauline, often 3-ranked, of a blade and sheath or sometimes the sheath only; sheath open or closed; ligule often present; blade usually linear and grass-like. Involucral bracts 1 to several, leaf-like or glume-like. Inflorescences unbranched and spicate or capitate, to branched and anthelate or paniculate, of one to many spikelets. Spikelets with 1 to many glumes, each glume subtending a single flower; glumes membranous to leathery, spirally arranged or 2-ranked. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, without a true perianth, this represented by bristles or scales or absent. Stamens usually 3. Ovary 1-locular with a single ovule; style 2- or 3-fid. Fruit a nutlet, trigonous or lenticular, in some genera enclosed in a sac-like perigynium.
families.philippine_note: CDFP accepts 200 Philippine species in 27 genera (Cyperus, Fimbristylis, Carex, Scleria, Eleocharis, Schoenoplectiella, Machaerina, Mapania, Rhynchospora, Bulbostylis, Paramapania, Schoenus, Fuirena, Hypolytrum, Isolepis, Schoenoplectus, Abildgaardia, Actinoschoenus, Actinoscirpus, Bolboschoenus, Cladium, Diplacrum, Gahnia, Lepironia, Scirpodendron, Scirpus, Trichophorum), 7 of them endemic (3.5%). One of the largest Philippine families by species but with very low endemism, reflecting the wide dispersal of sedges.

families.description: Trees or shrubs, evergreen, dioecious. Leaves simple, alternate and fasciculate, rarely opposite or subverticillate to verticillate, exstipulate; blades elliptic, oblong, obovate to ovate, frequently falcate or oblique, the apex rounded, mucronate, acute to acuminate, the base rounded to cuneate, the margins entire or revolute and infrequently dentate near the apex, chartaceous to coriaceous, usually glaucous and papillate beneath, the midrib frequently impressed above. Inflorescences axillary, rarely subterminal, racemiform, the axes angulate, terete or flat; bracts at the base of the inflorescence in one to several imbricate whorls, usually caducous and sometimes larger than the flower. Flowers unisexual. Calyx absent, or when present 3-6-lobed with imbricate aestivation, campanulate to cupulate or completely divided when mature.

families.description: Terrestrial plants, sometimes climbing. Rhizome usually long-creeping, usually covered with multicellular hairs, less often with few-celled cylindrical glandular hairs or multicellular bristles; SCALES ABSENT. Fronds medium-sized to large, sometimes of indeterminate growth, monomorphic; stipes not articulate to the rhizome, usually hairy; lamina 1-4-pinnately compound, thinly herbaceous to leathery, without scales; rachis grooved adaxially, sometimes bearing buds; pinnae opposite or alternate; veins usually free, pinnate or forked and not reaching the margin, reticulate in Histiopteris. Sori marginal or submarginal, protected by the reflexed leaf margin, by a true indusium, or by both.
families.philippine_note: CDFP accepts 36 Philippine species in 8 genera (Dennstaedtia, Hypolepis, Microlepia, Monachosorum, Paesia, Sitobolium, Histiopteris, Pteridium), 8 of them endemic (22.2%). Includes Pteridium, the bracken, one of the most widespread ferns in the Philippines and an aggressive coloniser of burnt and cleared ground.

families.description: Monoecious or dioecious trees, often scrambling shrubs, or lianas. Twigs and bark rather tough; medullary rays in the twigs many and distinct; pith rather small, usually dark-coloured and often disappearing early; wood rather hard. Stipules narrowly triangular to subulate, sometimes rather early caducous. Leaves spirally arranged. Flowers bisexual or unisexual, in Malesian species hypogynous or only slightly epigynous. Sepals ovate, imbricate, slightly confluent at the base, usually pubescent on both sides. Petals in Malesian species free, more or less spathulate, bifid to emarginate, creamy to white when fresh and dark when dried. Stamens 5, episepalous, free in Malesian species; anthers introrse.

families.description: Rhizomes, rarely spiny, producing annual and mostly twining shoots, in Malesia twining either to the right or to the left. Stems consisting of a main stem and sterile branches, both bearing leafless flowering axes. Leaves petiolate, generally cordate, simple and entire or palmately lobed, or palmately compound, triplinerved; apex generally glandular and developed before the blade as a forerunner tip; blade usually glandular beneath, chiefly towards the base. Flowers hermaphrodite or dioecious, actinomorphic, 3-merous, mostly inconspicuous and greenish, often massed and scented. Tepals in two whorls of 3. Stamens in 2 whorls of 3, the inner sometimes sterile; anthers usually introrse. Torus an urceolate perianthoid chamber in Stenomeris, a saucer or cup in many Dioscorea. Style 1 with 3 bifid stigmas. Ovary 3-locular, inferior. Ovules 2 in each cell or many in Stenomeris. Fruit a capsule. Seeds winged; endosperm horny.

families.description: Trees or shrubs with bisexual flowers or dioecious, semi-evergreen or deciduous. Stipules small, distinct, caducous. Leaves alternate, simple, petiolate. Inflorescences axillary on the current year's growth, of abbreviated cymes in a pedunculate umbel, or thyrses in a raceme or panicle. Flowers (4 or)5(-7)-merous, actinomorphic, only 1-4 mm across. Sepals and petals more or less undifferentiated and distinct. Stamens inserted at or within the margin of a disk; anthers introrse, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary superior. Fruit a drupaceous tardily dehiscent capsule with one seed, or a berry with 2-4 seeds. Seeds with or without an aril; endosperm present but thin.

families.description: Small to large resinous, usually evergreen trees, usually buttressed, and often with flaky or fissured bark when large. Some or most parts with a tomentum of fascicled hairs, or sometimes single hairs, unicellular or multicellular glandular hairs, or multicellular short or long lobed or peltate hairs. Leaves alternate, simple, the margin entire or sinuate and not crenate, terminating more or less abruptly at the prominent geniculate petiole, penninerved, often with domatia in the axils between the nerves and the midrib; tertiary nerves scalariform or reticulate. Stipules paired, large or small, persistent or fugaceous, leaving small to amplexicaul scars. Inflorescence paniculate, racemose or rarely cymose, more or less regularly branched, terminal or axillary; bracts and bracteoles paired.
families.philippine_note: CDFP accepts 54 Philippine species in 6 genera, 26 of them endemic (48.1%), and 33 of the 54 carry a DENR threatened-species listing - 14 as Critically Endangered. These are the lauan and apitong timbers on which Philippine forestry was built, and the conservation figures reflect what that cost. Ashton notes the family reaches its northern limit in Malesia at the Batan Islands north of Luzon.

families.description: Trees or erect shrubs, occasionally with spine-tipped branchlets. Leaves alternate, rarely opposite, entire; stipules absent. Flowers actinomorphic, usually unisexual with the plants dioecious or polygamous, rarely bisexual. Male flowers often in cymes, sometimes clustered or solitary, the pistil rudimentary or absent. Female flowers often solitary and axillary, without stamens or with imperfect ones. Calyx 3-7-lobed, persistent and often enlarging in female and bisexual flowers. Corolla 3-7-lobed, the lobes convolute. Stamens hypogynous or at the corolla base, 2-4 times as many as the corolla lobes, the filaments free or united in pairs. Ovary superior, 2-16-locular with 1 or 2 ovules per locule. Styles 2-8, free or basally united. Fruit a berry, seated on the enlarged persistent calyx.
families.philippine_note: CDFP accepts 35 Philippine species in 1 genus (Diospyros), 10 of them endemic (28.6%). The enlarged persistent calyx cupping the fruit is the field character. Diospyros includes the kamagong and Philippine ebony, among the most valuable and most depleted of Philippine timbers.

families.description: Trees or shrubs, evergreen or semi-evergreen. Leaves alternate or rarely opposite, stipulate or not, petiolate, simple, pinnately veined. Inflorescence axillary or terminal, racemose, corymbose or paniculate, or sometimes fascicled or of solitary flowers. Flowers bisexual or polygamous, 4- or 5-merous, actinomorphic, with or without bracts. Sepals 4 or 5, basally connate or free, usually valvate. Petals 4 or 5 and sometimes absent, valvate or imbricate, the margin laciniate - deeply fringed - or rarely entire. Stamens 8 to numerous, the filaments free and borne on a disk; anthers 2-celled, dehiscing by apical or longitudinal slits, awned or tipped with hairs. Disk circular or glandularly lobed. Ovary superior, 2- to several-locular with axile placentation and 2 to several ovules per locule; style connate or free. Fruit a drupe or capsule. Seeds with copious endosperm; embryo flat.
families.philippine_note: CDFP accepts 47 Philippine species in 2 genera (Elaeocarpus, Sloanea), 29 of them endemic (61.7%). The laciniate petal margin described here is the family's most distinctive floral character. Elaeocarpus accounts for nearly all the Philippine species, and the Flora Malesiana account of that genus was published only as a long series of precursor papers, never completed as a family treatment.

families.description: Annual herbs. Leaves stipulate, opposite or verticillate, simple. Flowers axillary, solitary, glomerate or fascicled, actinomorphic, small or minute. Sepals 2-5, free or shortly connate, imbricate in bud, pellucid or with pellucid margins, 1-nerved or nerveless, persistent. Petals as many as the sepals, scarcely surpassing them, imbricate in bud, free, membranous, persistent. Disk absent. Stamens as many as the petals and alternating with them, or more but not more than twice their number, persistent; anthers dorsifixed, small, 2-celled, dehiscing longitudinally. Ovary superior, 2-5-celled, the cells many-ovuled, the ovules on the inner angles. Styles as many as the cells, free, short, persistent. Capsule small, septicidal. Seeds many, minute, oblong, straight or curved, without endosperm.

families.description: Perennial or annual herbs. Leaves in a rosette, grass-like and linear, occasionally thinly filiform, often thin and transparent and fenestrate, the base sheathing. Inflorescences capitate, globose to ovoid; scapes thin, twisted and angled, the base surrounded by a bladeless tubular sheath. Flowers 2- or 3-merous, bracteate, with both sexes usually in the same head. Male flowers with 2 or 3 connate or free sepals, 2 or 3 often inconspicuous petals, and 6 stamens. Female flowers with 2 or 3 free or connate sepals, 0-4 free petals, a (1-)3-locular ovary with one basal ovule per locule, and a 1-3-branched style. Fruit a thin loculicidal capsule. Seeds small, the testa usually reticulate and prickly.

families.description: Shrubs or trees, the youngest branchlets compressed and older branches terete, the base of lateral twigs often bearing small distichous ramenta. Leaves simple, alternate and distichous, entire, involute in bud, the margins leaving two more or less permanent longitudinal lines on the upper surface. Stipules mostly entirely connate, intrapetiolar, often bicarinate, leaving a distinct oblique scar. Flowers axillary, solitary or clustered, often dimorphous or more, 5-merous, actinomorphic, bisexual. Calyx persistent, campanulate, divided about halfway into 5 imbricate lobes. Petals 5, free, caducous, quincuncial in bud, nearly always with an emarginate or 3-lobed ligule at the apex of the claw. Stamens 10 in two whorls of 5, persistent, the filaments connate below into a staminal tube. Ovary (1-)3-celled with one ovule per cell, normally only one cell fertile.

description.text: Shrubs or trees, the youngest branchlets compressed and older branches terete, the base of lateral twigs often bearing small distichous ramenta. Leaves simple, alternate and distichous, entire, involute in bud, the margins leaving two more or less permanent longitudinal lines on the upper surface. Stipules mostly entirely connate, intrapetiolar, often bicarinate, leaving a distinct oblique scar. Flowers axillary, solitary or clustered, often dimorphous or more, 5-merous, actinomorphic, bisexual. Calyx persistent, campanulate, divided about halfway into 5 imbricate lobes. Petals 5, free, caducous, quincuncial in bud, nearly always with an emarginate or 3-lobed ligule at the apex of the claw. Stamens 10 in two whorls of 5, persistent, the filaments connate below into a staminal tube. Ovary (1-)3-celled with one ovule per cell, normally only one cell fertile.

Leaves alternate or opposite, rarely whorled; stipules usually present, often free, sometimes modified into spines or glands; petioles sometimes with glands at apex or base; blade simple and sometimes palmately lobed, rarely compound or reduced to scales, the margin entire or toothed and sometimes with distinct glands, the venation pinnate or palmate. Inflorescences axillary or terminal, the flowers in cymes or fascicles often arranged along an elongated axis to form a thyrse, in congested heads, or in a flower-like cyathium in which very reduced flowers are enclosed in a cupular involucre; bracts sometimes petaloid. Flowers unisexual, actinomorphic. Sepals (1-)3-6(-8), free or connate, valvate or imbricate, rarely absent in Euphorbia. Petals free, often reduced or absent. Disc present or absent. Stamens one to very many, hypogynous, the filaments free or connate. Ovary superior, usually 3-locular with one or two ovules per locule. Fruit usually a schizocarpic capsule splitting explosively into 3 cocci.

families.description: Trees, shrubs or herbs, sometimes climbing or decumbent, very often bearing root nodules that harbour nitrogen-fixing bacteria. Leaves alternate or rarely opposite, pinnate or bipinnate, less often palmately compound or 3-foliolate, seldom 1-foliolate or simple, or modified into narrow phyllodes; stipules and stipels present or absent, the stipules sometimes developed into spines. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual, actinomorphic in Mimosoideae, more or less zygomorphic in Caesalpinioideae, and strongly zygomorphic in Papilionoideae, mostly in racemes, corymbs, spikes, heads or panicles. Sepals (3-)5(or 6), free or connate into a tube and sometimes bilabiate. Petals (0-)5(or 6), imbricate or valvate, in the papilionaceous corolla highly differentiated into an outermost upper petal (the standard), two more or less parallel lateral petals (the wings), and two innermost lower petals usually connate along their lower margins to form a keel. Stamens mostly 10, sometimes fewer or more, distinct or often connate by their filaments into a closed or open sheath, monadelphous or diadelphous; anthers 2-locular, opening lengthwise or by pores. Gynoecium nearly always of a solitary carpel; ovary superior, 1-locular or sometimes transversely septate; ovules 1 to numerous on the adaxial suture. Fruit a legume, dehiscent by one or both sutures, or indehiscent, sometimes winged, sometimes jointed and breaking into one-seeded segments. Seeds with little or no endosperm, sometimes strophiolate.

description.text: Trees, shrubs or herbs, sometimes climbing or decumbent, very often bearing root nodules that harbour nitrogen-fixing bacteria. Leaves alternate or rarely opposite, pinnate or bipinnate, less often palmately compound or 3-foliolate, seldom 1-foliolate or simple, or modified into narrow phyllodes; stipules and stipels present or absent, the stipules sometimes developed into spines. Flowers bisexual, rarely unisexual, actinomorphic in Mimosoideae, more or less zygomorphic in Caesalpinioideae, and strongly zygomorphic in Papilionoideae, mostly in racemes, corymbs, spikes, heads or panicles. Sepals (3-)5(or 6), free or connate into a tube and sometimes bilabiate. Petals (0-)5(or 6), imbricate or valvate, in the papilionaceous corolla highly differentiated into an outermost upper petal (the standard), two more or less parallel lateral petals (the wings), and two innermost lower petals usually connate along their lower margins to form a keel. Stamens mostly 10, sometimes fewer or more, distinct or often connate by their filaments into a closed or open sheath, monadelphous or diadelphous; anthers 2-locular, opening lengthwise or by pores. Gynoecium nearly always of a solitary carpel; ovary superior, 1-locular or sometimes transversely septate; ovules 1 to numerous on the adaxial suture. Fruit a legume, dehiscent by one or both sutures, or indehiscent, sometimes winged, sometimes jointed and breaking into one-seeded segments. Seeds with little or no endosperm, sometimes strophiolate.

Characters universal in Chinese material may vary in Philippine material, and Philippine genera absent from China are not covered at all.

families.description: Erect, ascending, climbing or floating perennials, often robust, stoloniferous or not. Leaves spirally arranged or bifarious, subsessile or distinctly stalked, ovate-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate or linear, with or without a spirally coiled tendril-like apex; sheaths embracing the stem, closed all round or more or less deeply split on the anterior side. Blade closely longitudinally nerved or subpenninerved, the nerves connected by numerous short and often oblique transverse veinlets. Flowers in terminal sessile or peduncled panicles, sessile, actinomorphic, bisexual or unisexual, rather small. Perianth hypogynous. Tepals 6, biseriately imbricate, free or shortly connate, persistent. Stamens 6, free; anthers basifixed, 2-celled, the cells bursting by an introrse longitudinal slit. Ovary superior, sessile, 3-celled, each cell with a solitary ovule in the inner angle; stigmas 3 or one deeply 3-lobed stigma, sessile. Fruit drupaceous, indehiscent. Seeds 1-3; albumen copious; embryo small.

Inflorescences usually cymes, rarely racemes, axillary and often near the apex so as to appear terminal, usually pedunculate. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic and seldom actinomorphic. Calyx actinomorphic and rarely zygomorphic, usually (4 or)5-divided. Corolla gamopetalous, zygomorphic and rarely actinomorphic, usually 2-lipped. Fertile stamens 2 or 4 and then often didynamous, rarely 5, epipetalous; anthers free or coherent, the thecae 2 and parallel, divergent or divaricate; staminodes 1-3 or absent. Disc ring-like to cupular, rarely absent. Ovary superior in all Old World taxa, 1-locular, rarely 2-locular; placentas (1 or)2, parietal; ovules numerous. Style 1; stigmas 1 or 2. Fruit usually a capsule dehiscing loculicidally, septicidally or circumscissilely, rarely a berry or indehiscent. Seeds numerous, minute, fusiform to ellipsoid or ovoid, sometimes appendaged at one or both ends.

families.description: Glabrous trees, shrubs or, for the most part, vines. Leaves decussate, simple, entire, penninerved and exstipulate, usually with fine pellucid lines of spicular cells running parallel to the secondary veins, the leaf then bearded on fracture. Spikes simple or branched, axillary or often cauline, dioecious, each with two opposite basal scales and several collars containing moniliform hairs and sessile flowers: either numerous spirally arranged male flowers below a ring of sterile female flowers, or a ring of few fertile female flowers. Male flower a claw-shaped, transversely splitting perianth with a central stamen bearing two apical yellow microsporangia opening by an apical median slit. Female flower with a fleshy outer envelope and two thin inner ones, the innermost drawn into a long slender apical tube, enclosing an orthotropous ovule. Fruit usually pink, consisting of the fleshy outer envelope, sometimes narrowed into a stalk, a hardened ribbed middle envelope, a thin silky inner envelope, and a large horny seed with a small embryo.
families.philippine_note: CDFP accepts 4 species of Gnetum for the Philippines, one of them endemic. All Malesian species occur in tropical rain forest below about 1500 m.
families.scope_note: Flora Malesiana treats the family directly under its single genus Gnetum, which is also the only genus in the Philippines.

families.description: Perennial, caulescent, rhizomatous herbs with fasciculate fibrous roots, sometimes stoloniferous, rarely with rounded tubers. Leaves radical, equitant, linear or ensiform, strongly laterally compressed in the manner of an Iris, with an open or closed amplexicaul sheathing base, closely striate-nerved or plicate-nerved. Flowers in Malesian species actinomorphic, paniculate. Perianth segments 6, biseriate, free. Stamens 3, epipetalous; anthers 2-celled, basifixed or versatile, introrse, splitting lengthwise. Ovary superior to inferior, 3-celled. Style simple, usually filiform; stigma punctiform. Ovules few to many per cell, on axile placentas. Capsule loculicidal, 3-valved. Seeds with abundant endosperm and a small embryo, often flat and sometimes winged.

description.text: Perennial, caulescent, rhizomatous herbs with fasciculate fibrous roots, sometimes stoloniferous, rarely with rounded tubers. Leaves radical, equitant, linear or ensiform, strongly laterally compressed in the manner of an Iris, with an open or closed amplexicaul sheathing base, closely striate-nerved or plicate-nerved. Flowers in Malesian species actinomorphic, paniculate. Perianth segments 6, biseriate, free. Stamens 3, epipetalous; anthers 2-celled, basifixed or versatile, introrse, splitting lengthwise. Ovary superior to inferior, 3-celled. Style simple, usually filiform; stigma punctiform. Ovules few to many per cell, on axile placentas. Capsule loculicidal, 3-valved. Seeds with abundant endosperm and a small embryo, often flat and sometimes winged.

families.description: Evergreen or deciduous shrubs or trees. Buds perulate or naked; innovations flush-wise. Leaves simple, spirally arranged and rarely opposite, usually penninerved and less often 3-5-plinerved, the margins entire, crenate-serrate or dentate, often slightly oblique at the base. Indumentum often stellate, tufted or lepidote. Stipules usually present, very small to large. Flowers free or connate, in heads, spikes or racemes, bisexual, polygamous, or unisexual and monoecious, usually actinomorphic and 4-5-merous. Sepals usually small or lacking. Petals often linear or ligulate, often rolled in bud, sometimes lacking. Stamens free, often in two whorls with the inner staminodial; anthers almost always basifixed, the connective often produced. Ovary of 2, exceptionally 3, carpels often free at the apex, 2-celled, usually more or less inferior; styles 2, free, long and often recurved, frequently persistent and hardened in fruit. Capsules 2-celled, usually loculicidal and septicidal.

families.description: Trees, shrubs, or woody climbers, with bisexual or unisexual flowers. Leaves alternate or spirally arranged, petiolate, without stipules, simple and lobed or unlobed, or palmately compound, the margin entire. Inflorescences usually axillary, much-branched compound cymes, sometimes corymbose, with or without bracts. Perianth sepaloid, of 3-8 imbricate or valvate tepals in one or two whorls. Stamens 3-7 in a single whorl opposite the tepals, or in a double whorl inserted opposite the outer tepals; filaments with two basal glands, or one dorsal gland, or none; anthers 2-locular, dehiscing by two lateral or apical valves; interstaminal staminodes present or absent. Ovary inferior, 1-locular; ovule 1, pendulous; style simple; stigma discoid and oblique.

Inflorescences usually axillary, much-branched compound cymes, sometimes corymbose, with or without bracts. Perianth sepaloid, of 3-8 imbricate or valvate tepals in one or two whorls. Stamens 3-7 in a single whorl opposite the tepals, or in a double whorl inserted opposite the outer tepals; filaments with two basal glands, or one dorsal gland, or none; anthers 2-locular, dehiscing by two lateral or apical valves; interstaminal staminodes present or absent. Ovary inferior, 1-locular; ovule 1, pendulous; style simple; stigma discoid and oblique.

families.description: Annual or perennial, unarmed or spinous, bitter herbs or undershrubs, often glandular-hairy. Stem terete, farctate, with a peripheral whorl of air vessels. Leaves spread, simple, entire, exstipulate. Flowers actinomorphic, solitary and opposite or between the leaves, or through reduction of the leaves more or less arranged in a racemiform or paniculiform inflorescence, distinctly pedicelled, lilac-blue. Calyx persistent, 5-partite nearly to the base, the segments lanceolate and imbricate in bud, not or hardly accrescent after anthesis. Corolla sympetalous, deeply 5-partite, the limb rotate, the segments imbricate in bud, oval and obtuse. Stamens 5, free, inserted in the throat of the corolla and alternating with the segments; filaments filiform from a broadened base; anthers 2-celled, bifid at base and apex, opening lengthwise.

families.description: Perennial ferns of usually small size. Rhizome long- or short-creeping, less often ascending or erect, bearing hairs and lacking scales, with a so-called Hymenophyllaceae-protostele. Fronds simple to pinnately decompound, or simple dichotomous or seemingly digitate; stipes not joined to the rhizome, terete, with a single leaf trace, hairy or becoming glabrous; laminae unistratose except on the veins and sori, or two- to four-stratose without intercellular spaces and stomata. Fronds range from a few millimetres to more than 50 cm long, and are attached basipetally even when simple.

families.description: Trees, shrubs, or perennial or annual herbs. Leaves simple, in Malesian species opposite and decussate and entire, sessile to shortly petioled, often with translucent and sometimes black or red glandular dots or lines. Stipules absent. Inflorescences terminal and sometimes axillary, very rarely axillary only, cymose to thyrsoid or rarely racemose, bracteate at least initially. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, homostylous or heterodistylous. Sepals 5 in Malesian species, free or more or less united, imbricate, glandular like the leaves, persistent. Petals 5, free, imbricate and contorted, alternisepalous, usually glandular, sometimes with a nectariferous basal appendage. Stamen fascicles 5, epipetalous, free or variously united, each with one to many stamens; anthers 2-thecal, dorsifixed, often with a gland terminating the connective. Ovary superior, 5-3-celled, or 1-celled with 5-2 parietal placentas; styles 5-3.

families.description: Trees, climbing or non-climbing shrubs, or lianas. Leaves spirally arranged, rarely opposite, simple, entire or lobed, in Malesia never crenate or serrate, penni- or palmatinerved, exstipulate. Inflorescences mostly axillary, sometimes terminal, rarely extra-axillary or from the old wood, in spikes or spike-like racemes, or often in cymes, both spikes and cymes not rarely collected into panicles or heads, very rarely reduced to few-flowered fascicles or a solitary flower. Flowers bisexual or unisexual and then the plants dioecious, actinomorphic, (4-)5(-6)-merous, rarely in part 3-merous by reduction, cyclic with sepals and petals or rarely with petals only or without petals. Pedicels, where present, articulated with the calyx. Sepals 4-6, free or mostly connate below into a 4-6-lobed calyx, the lobes imbricate or valvate, generally persistent. Petals 4-6, free or connate below, sometimes into a tube, the lobes valvate and very rarely subimbricate, the tip inflexed, mostly caducous.

families.description: Herbaceous perennial submerged aquatics or marsh plants, usually with annual grass-like leaves arising in a tuft from a lobed, flattened, corm-like stock, the stock divided into stem and rhizophore and 2-4-lobed, with black dichotomous roots arising from the furrows between the lobes. Roots monarch, the stele attached to one side of a central cavity. Leaves distichous, crowded, with overlapping bases, terete or flattened above, with a broad spoon-like base; blades with a single unbranched median vein, the mesophyll chambered with four longitudinal cavities divided by transverse diaphragms, which gives the leaf a muriform appearance in transmitted light. Leaf bases usually membranaceous and hyaline, in some species persisting as hard brown 2-lobed horny structures. Ligule present near the leaf base above the sporangium, arising from a ligular pit, cordate-triangular to subulate, 2-15 mm long.

description.text: Herbaceous perennial submerged aquatics or marsh plants, usually with annual grass-like leaves arising in a tuft from a lobed, flattened, corm-like stock, the stock divided into stem and rhizophore and 2-4-lobed, with black dichotomous roots arising from the furrows between the lobes. Roots monarch, the stele attached to one side of a central cavity. Leaves distichous, crowded, with overlapping bases, terete or flattened above, with a broad spoon-like base; blades with a single unbranched median vein, the mesophyll chambered with four longitudinal cavities divided by transverse diaphragms, which gives the leaf a muriform appearance in transmitted light. Leaf bases usually membranaceous and hyaline, in some species persisting as hard brown 2-lobed horny structures. Ligule present near the leaf base above the sporangium, arising from a ligular pit, cordate-triangular to subulate, 2-15 mm long.
description.note: Description of the family as treated for Malesia, the region containing the Philippines.

families.description: Evergreen, buttressed trees or treelets, growing monopodially in flushes, glabrous. Bark brownish, finely fissured, rich in tannin. Stipules caducous, free, scale-like, obliquely triangular. Leaves simple, spirally arranged, the margin slightly thickened and entire or glandular-serrate, pinnately nerved, mostly obovate and tapering to a short petiole. Inflorescences axillary, dichasially corymbose, the bracts scale-like and persistent, bracteoles absent. Flowers bisexual, 5-merous, actinomorphic, perigynous, the young buds sticky; calyx and corolla indurated and enlarging, persistent in fruit. Sepals connate at the base, quincuncial; petals quincuncial, almost free, distinctly veined. Stamens 10 or (15-)20 in one whorl. Disk well developed, bowl-shaped, with a free erect margin. Ovary superior, 5-celled, with 2 pendulous ovules per locule; style 1, the stigma mushroom-shaped. Capsule septicidal and septifragal, 5-valved, without a central column. Seeds 1 or 2 per cell, with a basal wing or a suprahilar arillode; endosperm spongy, oily.

families.description: Perennial or annual herbs, tufted or with an erect or creeping rhizome. Stems mostly leafy only at the base, sometimes also above. Leaves spirally arranged, cylindric to flat and grass-like, mostly linear or filiform, sheathing at the base or entirely reduced to a sheath; sheaths open or closed, sometimes ciliate at the top. Flowers mostly protogynous and wind-pollinated, solitary or in anthelas, panicles, corymbs or heads, usually small, actinomorphic. Tepals 6, free, in two whorls, rarely only 3, glumaceous or coriaceous. Stamens 3-6, when 3 opposite the outer tepals; anthers basifixed, introrse, the cells opening longitudinally; pollen in tetrads. Ovary superior, 1-celled or divided by 3 septa into 3 cells; style short to long; stigmas 3, papillose; ovules 3 at the base of the ovary, or numerous and biseriate on 3 parietal placentas. Fruit a dry 1- or 3-celled capsule, loculicidally 3-valved. Seeds sometimes tailed.

families.description: Trees, shrubs, subshrubs, perennial or annual herbs or climbers, aromatic or not. Stems often quadrangular, erect to prostrate, sometimes forming stolons or rhizomes. Indumentum usually present, of glandular and non-glandular trichomes, usually multicellular-uniseriate, simple, branched, dendroid or stellate, sometimes gland-tipped; large-headed subsessile glands rarely absent. Leaves opposite and often decussate, sometimes whorled, very rarely alternate, simple, entire, toothed or lobed, sometimes palmate, petiolate or sessile, exstipulate. Inflorescences often bracteate, composed of cymes and often arranged in a terminal lax or congested indeterminate thyrse, this paniculate, raceme-like, spike-like, or rarely congested into a capitulum. Flowers hypogynous, usually bisexual, actinomorphic to more often slightly or strongly zygomorphic, often 2-lipped. Calyx actinomorphic to zygomorphic, sometimes 2-lipped, the lobes 2 to many and often 5, equal or unequal, often accrescent and rarely inflated or fleshy in fruit. Corolla with the petals connate, rarely 1-lipped, the lobes (2-)4-5(-16). Stamens epipetalous, usually 4 or 2 by abortion with staminodes often present, when 4 often didynamous; anthers usually dithecous, or monothecous by abortion.

description.text: Trees, shrubs, subshrubs, perennial or annual herbs or climbers, aromatic or not. Stems often quadrangular, erect to prostrate, sometimes forming stolons or rhizomes. Indumentum usually present, of glandular and non-glandular trichomes, usually multicellular-uniseriate, simple, branched, dendroid or stellate, sometimes gland-tipped; large-headed subsessile glands rarely absent. Leaves opposite and often decussate, sometimes whorled, very rarely alternate, simple, entire, toothed or lobed, sometimes palmate, petiolate or sessile, exstipulate. Inflorescences often bracteate, composed of cymes and often arranged in a terminal lax or congested indeterminate thyrse, this paniculate, raceme-like, spike-like, or rarely congested into a capitulum. Flowers hypogynous, usually bisexual, actinomorphic to more often slightly or strongly zygomorphic, often 2-lipped. Calyx actinomorphic to zygomorphic, sometimes 2-lipped, the lobes 2 to many and often 5, equal or unequal, often accrescent and rarely inflated or fleshy in fruit. Corolla with the petals connate, rarely 1-lipped, the lobes (2-)4-5(-16). Stamens epipetalous, usually 4 or 2 by abortion with staminodes often present, when 4 often didynamous; anthers usually dithecous, or monothecous by abortion.

families.description: Trees or shrubs, with Cassytha a twining parasitic perennial herb whose leaves are reduced or absent; mostly evergreen, sometimes dioecious. Bark and foliage usually aromatic. Leaves usually alternate, occasionally opposite, subopposite or whorled, simple and usually entire, mostly pinninerved and subpalmately veined or often triplinerved, usually punctate and leathery, exstipulate. Flowers in usually axillary, occasionally subterminal panicles, spikes, racemes or pseudo-umbels, generally bisexual and sometimes unisexual, actinomorphic, mostly 3-merous, small, greenish, yellowish or white. Perianth biseriate of usually 4 or 6 basally connate and undifferentiated sepal-like segments, deciduous or persistent, the tube usually persisting as a cupule at the fruit base. Androecium typically of four whorls of three stamens adnate to the perianth tube, the innermost whorl usually reduced to staminodes; the third whorl usually bearing two sessile basal glands; anthers basifixed, 2- or 4-celled at anthesis, the outer two whorls mostly introrse and the third whorl extrorse, dehiscing by flap-like valves opening upwards. Ovary usually superior, 1-locular with a solitary pendulous ovule; style 1. Fruit a drupe or berry, usually seated at the base in the enlarged and often persistent perianth tube on a large receptacle or pedicel. Seed with a large straight embryo; endosperm absent.

families.description: Small to large trees, rarely shrubs, pachycaul or leptocaul. Leaves alternate or spirally arranged in whorls at the apex of the branches, simple, the margins entire or serrate-crenulate, pinnately nerved and usually brochidodromous; stipules absent or minute and caducous. Inflorescences terminal, axillary or cauline, simple and often pendulous racemes, or panicles in Chydenanthus and Petersianthus, or rarely the flowers solitary; bracts and bracteoles usually small and caducous. Flowers actinomorphic, hermaphrodite, sessile or pedicellate. Calyx tube most frequently campanulate or conical, very rarely winged; sepals 2-6, often circumscissile. Petals 3-5, free, most often 4, imbricate. Stamens numerous, in 3-8(-12) whorls, usually far-exserted, connate at the base into a short actinomorphic staminal ring, the inner whorls often staminodal; anthers bilocular, dehiscing longitudinally. Disc an intrastaminal annular ring. Ovary inferior, usually 2-4-locular with 2-6 anatropous ovules per locule, the ovules attached apically or axially and basally in Chydenanthus; style slender.

families.description: Herbs, usually glabrous, with perennial underground stems - corms, bulbs, tubers or rhizomes - in all Malesian species. Leaves simple, caespitose and basal, sometimes distichous, or if cauline usually alternate, generally linear to lanceolate or oblanceolate when basal but sometimes shorter and broader when cauline, usually sessile, usually with parallel venation. Perianth segments almost invariably 6 in two similar or distinctly dissimilar whorls of 3, petaloid, connate or free, the outer whorl sometimes saccate at the base. families.description: Trees, shrubs, woody climbers or herbs. Hairs simple, stellate, or glandular-capitate; colleters often present in the axils of the leaves, stipules and sepals. Leaves nearly always opposite, entire or nearly so, penninerved, rarely 3-7-plinerved in Strychnos. Flowers 4-5(up to 16)-merous, nearly always bisexual, actinomorphic or in some genera slightly zygomorphic. Sepals united or free. Corolla gamopetalous, very rarely with a corona. Stamens isomerous in Malesian species, alternating with the corolla lobes and inserted on the tube, included or exserted; anthers basifixed or sometimes slightly dorsifixed. Ovary superior, or semi-inferior in a few genera, (1-)2(-4)-celled, the placentas axile or parietal if 1-celled and often peltate; ovules one to many per cell; style usually one. Fruit always superior, capsular, baccate or drupaceous. Seeds 1 to many, with copious endosperm.

families.description: Large plants, terrestrial, climbing or epiphytic. Rhizomes stout, ascending or long-scandent, dorsiventral with roots on the ventral side and several rows of fronds on the dorsal side, bearing numerous scales at the apex. Fronds distant, monomorphic or dimorphic, imparipinnate; stipes densely scaly at the base, the scales black and lanceolate or linear; lateral pinnae articulate to the rachis; sterile pinnae linear-lanceolate with entire or serrate margins; veins free or anastomosing in several rows of areoles without included free veinlets. Fertile fronds with narrow linear pinnae. Sori dorsal on the veinlets in 1-4 rows each side of the costa, or acrostichoid and completely covering the abaxial surface, exindusiate.

description.text: Large plants, terrestrial, climbing or epiphytic. Rhizomes stout, ascending or long-scandent, dorsiventral with roots on the ventral side and several rows of fronds on the dorsal side, bearing numerous scales at the apex. Fronds distant, monomorphic or dimorphic, imparipinnate; stipes densely scaly at the base, the scales black and lanceolate or linear; lateral pinnae articulate to the rachis; sterile pinnae linear-lanceolate with entire or serrate margins; veins free or anastomosing in several rows of areoles without included free veinlets. Fertile fronds with narrow linear pinnae. Sori dorsal on the veinlets in 1-4 rows each side of the costa, or acrostichoid and completely covering the abaxial surface, exindusiate.

families.description: Perennial evergreen hemiparasites, usually aerial stem-parasitic shrubs, sometimes terrestrial root-parasitic shrubs or trees; attachment to the host in aerial stem-parasites by many haustoria produced on epicortical runners, especially in Malesia, or by a single complex woody primary haustorium. Leaves mostly opposite, less often alternate or verticillate, always simple; stipules absent. Inflorescences mostly axillary, less often terminal, internodal, or borne on the epicortical runners; the uniflorescence a simple dichasium or a single flower, these usually aggregated into racemose, umbellate or capitate compound inflorescences. Flowers dichlamydeous, mostly hermaphrodite, the plants mostly dioecious when unisexual. Calyx a membranous limb at the apex of the ovary, without vascular bundles. Corolla choripetalous or gamopetalous, regular or somewhat zygomorphic, normally 4- to 6-merous, valvate. Stamens as many as and opposite the petals, epipetalous; anthers mostly basifixed, immobile and continuous with the filament, sometimes dorsifixed and then usually versatile, opening by longitudinal slits. Ovary inferior, the ovarian cavity with or without a central column.

Main stems creeping, pendulous, climbing, or short and erect, on the substrate surface or subterranean, or forming stolons. Sporangia solitary in the leaf axils, reniform, opening by a transverse slit; spores all of one kind.

families.description: Terrestrial plants. Stems branched and slender; fronds often several metres long, alternately pinnate, CLIMBING BY MEANS OF A TWINING RACHIS - the frond itself is the climbing organ and grows indefinitely, which is unique among Philippine ferns. Primary pinnae pseudodichotomously forking with a dormant apical bud in the axil; pinnules entire to palmately or 1- or 2-pinnately divided; fertile and sterile pinnae similar, or the fertile greatly contracted; veins free or anastomosing. Sori on the lobes of the ultimate segments; sporangia abaxial and solitary, one per sorus, each covered by an antrorse indusium-like flange; spores tetrahedral and trilete; gametophytes green, cordate and terrestrial.

families.description: Trees or shrubs, glabrous or with an indumentum of single hairs. Leaves spirally arranged, simple, entire or 2-10-lobed, penninerved, evergreen or deciduous; stipules present, at first enclosing and protecting the innovations, later caducous and leaving an annular scar around the node. Flowers terminal or pseudo-axillary on a short shoot, bisexual and rarely unisexual, pedunculate; peduncle bearing one or more caducous spathaceous bracts that leave annular scars. Perianth spiral or spirocyclic, simple or differentiated into calyx and corolla, of 6 or more free imbricate members. Stamens numerous, free, spirally arranged; anthers linear, 2-locular, the connective usually produced into an appendage. Gynoecium sessile or stipitate; carpels numerous to few, rarely one, spirally arranged, free or sometimes concrescent; ovules 2 or more, biseriate on the ventral suture. Fruit apocarpous, sometimes syncarpous, the fruiting carpels opening along the dorsal and/or ventral suture, or circumscissile, rarely indehiscent. Seeds large, in dehiscent carpels hanging from the elongated spiral vessels of the funicle, with an arilloid testa.

families.description: Herbs, shrubs or less often trees; indumentum usually of peltate scales or stellate hairs. Leaves alternate, stipulate, petiolate; blade usually palmately veined, entire or variously lobed. Flowers solitary, less often in small cymes or clusters, axillary or subterminal and often aggregated into terminal racemes or panicles, usually conspicuous, actinomorphic, usually bisexual. Epicalyx often present, forming an involucre of 3 to many lobes around the calyx. Sepals 5, valvate, free or connate. Petals 5, free, contorted or imbricate, adnate at the base to the base of the filament tube. Stamens usually very many, the filaments connate into a tube around the style; anthers 1-celled. Pollen spiny. Ovary superior of 2-25 carpels, these often separating from one another and from the axis; styles as many as or twice as many as the carpels. Fruit a capsule or a schizocarp of mericarps.

families.description: Perennial rhizomatous herbs, aerial stems present or absent. Leaves distichous and usually large; petiole sheathing at the base and with a swollen pulvinus at the apex - the joint that lets the blade turn to follow the light, and the readiest character for the family; blade pinnately veined, the lateral veins parallel and slightly S-shaped. Inflorescences terminal or axillary, borne on leafy shoots or occasionally on separate leafless shoots from the rhizome, compound, head-like, spicate or diffuse and much branched, bracteate, each bract subtending a pair of flowers or a cincinnus of paired flowers. Flowers bisexual, asymmetric, paired or rarely single. Sepals 3, free. Corolla lobes 3, often slightly unequal, basally connate into a tube. Staminodes and stamen in two whorls: the outer of 1 or 2 petaloid staminodes, the inner of a hooded staminode enclosing the style at anthesis and a single fertile stamen bearing a lateral anther. Ovary inferior. Fruit a capsule or berry.

families.description: Terrestrial, rarely epiphytic, evergreen plants. Rhizomes erect, ascending or creeping, starchy. Fronds monomorphic and long-lived, simple or compound, 1-4-pinnate or palmate, from about 20 cm to at least 6 m long. Stipes fleshy, with a pair of stipule-like appendages at the base, often with conspicuous lenticels. Pulvini present at the frond base, at the nodes, and at the bases of the pinnae. Veins free and simple or bifurcate, or reticulate in Christensenia, with false veins sometimes present between the true veins. Tissues mucilaginous. Indumentum of multicellular uniseriate hairs and basifixed or peltate scales. Sori lacking true indusia, usually with paraphyses, superficial, sunken or stalked, elongate along the veins. SPORANGIA PARTIALLY OR COMPLETELY FUSED INTO SYNANGIA, dehiscing by a slit or pore.
families.philippine_note: CDFP accepts 12 Philippine species in 3 genera (Angiopteris, Ptisana, Christensenia), 1 of them endemic (8.3%). The fused synangia and the fleshy stipules at the frond base separate this ancient family from all other Philippine ferns.

description.text: Terrestrial, rarely epiphytic, evergreen plants. Rhizomes erect, ascending or creeping, starchy. Fronds monomorphic and long-lived, simple or compound, 1-4-pinnate or palmate, from about 20 cm to at least 6 m long. Stipes fleshy, with a pair of stipule-like appendages at the base, often with conspicuous lenticels. Pulvini present at the frond base, at the nodes, and at the bases of the pinnae. Veins free and simple or bifurcate, or reticulate in Christensenia, with false veins sometimes present between the true veins. Tissues mucilaginous. Indumentum of multicellular uniseriate hairs and basifixed or peltate scales. Sori lacking true indusia, usually with paraphyses, superficial, sunken or stalked, elongate along the veins. SPORANGIA PARTIALLY OR COMPLETELY FUSED INTO SYNANGIA, dehiscing by a slit or pore.

families.description: Rhizomes creeping, dorsiventral, polycyclic-solenostelic, densely covered with light-brown or brown hairs. Leaves alternate on the dorsal side of the rhizome; stipes polished, glabrous; lamina either pedate with pectinate pinnae, or alternately pinnate with the pinnae consisting of resting buds or bud-derived leaflets and linear simple or forked pinnules; veins free or anastomosing in the soriferous parts. Spores tetrahedral, trilete.

families.description: Herbs, shrubs or trees to 20 m, erect, climbing or rarely epiphytic. Stipules lacking. Leaves simple, commonly opposite and decussate with one of each pair slightly smaller than the other, rarely verticillate or alternate; venation acrodromous, with the secondary veins running from base to apex more or less parallel to the margin and the tertiary veins reticulate between them - the character by which the family is recognised in the field. Inflorescences cymose, umbellate, corymbose, in paniculate clusters or a cincinnus, rarely the flowers single, fascicled or spicate. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic though the androecium is often slightly zygomorphic, usually (3 or)4- or 5(or 6)-merous, the perianth biseriate, perigynous. Hypanthium funnel-shaped, campanulate, cyathiform or urceolate. Calyx lobes (3-)5(or 6), valvate. Petals (3-)5(or 6), distinct, imbricate. Stamens usually twice as many as the petals in two whorls, rarely as many by loss of a whorl, isomorphic or dimorphic; filaments distinct and often geniculate, inflexed in bud; anthers typically 2-celled, introrse, basifixed, dehiscing by one or two apical pores or short longitudinal slits.
families.philippine_note: CDFP accepts 198 Philippine species in 18 genera (Medinilla, Memecylon, Astronia, Melastoma, Dissochaeta, Beccarianthus, Creochiton, Sonerila, Diplectria, Anerincleistus, Astrocalyx, Catanthera, Heterotis, Lijndenia, Miconia, Ochthocharis, Osbeckia, Sarcopyramis), 160 of them endemic (80.8%). The acrodromous venation described here is what makes this family recognisable without flowers, and holds across Philippine material.
